jobs.title: Data Scientist, Enterprise
jobs.description:
Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.

About The Role

Replit spreads through companies differently than it does through individuals. One person builds an app, colleagues start using it, a team forms, an admin rolls Replit out more widely, and eventually Sales gets involved. You'll be the data scientist for Replit's enterprise business, covering both the product and the go-to-market motion: how Replit spreads inside organizations, what keeps teams engaged after rollout, which features and signals drive expansion, and how all of that becomes pipeline, revenue, and a reliable forecast.

Experimentation is hard here. There are far fewer accounts than users, people within an organization influence each other, and admins control what their teams see. You'll figure out how to learn quickly and rigorously anyway. You'll work with Enterprise Product, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, RevOps, and Finance, and your work succeeds when it changes a product, GTM, or investment decision.

You Will

Define how we measure the enterprise business end to end: account-level activation, breadth (share of seats active), depth (apps built, deployed, and shared), collaboration, consumption, and net revenue retention
Understand virality inside organizations: how Replit spreads from a first builder to teams through app sharing, invites, and viewers who become builders; quantify within-account network effects and find the levers that accelerate them
Explain post-engagement churn: why seats and accounts that engaged at rollout go dormant, separate seat-level decay from account-level risk, and turn it into account health models that give the product and Customer Success early warning and a clear next action
Identify the product behaviors and features that precede seat expansion and plan upgrades, and use them to build product-qualified account (PQA) models that route bottoms-up usage to Sales at the right moment
Measure adoption and value for enterprise features — admin and governance controls, security, data connectors, collaboration, and deploying to data platforms — and use it to inform what we build next
Design experiments for enterprise: account- and cluster-level randomization, interference within organizations, small samples and heavy-tailed account sizes, stratified and matched-pair designs, staged rollouts and long-running holdouts, synthetic control, and Bayesian or hierarchical models where data is sparse
Measure the incremental impact of GTM programs — pilots, onboarding, enablement, and sales-assist — with the same rigor as product launches
Own enterprise forecasting for pipeline, bookings, consumption, and expansion, and pressure-test the assumptions behind capacity and quota plans
Analyze pricing and packaging: seats vs. consumption, and how contract structure shapes usage
Build a trusted enterprise data layer that joins product telemetry, CRM, and billing data and models the org, workspace, team, and seat hierarchy, so Product, Sales, and leadership can self-serve — increasingly through AI agents rather than static dashboards
Bring a point of view to the enterprise roadmap and GTM strategy before you're asked

Required Skills And Experience

6+ years in product or GTM data science, with significant experience on B2B, collaboration, or multi-seat products
Hands-on experimentation where the unit of randomization differs from the unit of analysis: cluster randomization, interference, and small-sample designs
Strong retention and survival modeling, cohort analysis, and segmentation at both user and account level
Experience defining adoption, retention, and revenue metrics (activation, NRR, GRR, expansion) and getting the company to agree on them
Built scoring or forecasting models that Sales, Customer Success, or Finance actually used
Expert SQL, including messy CRM, billing, and product data joined at the account level; strong Python; comfortable building your own datasets in dbt
A track record of analysis that changed a product roadmap or GTM decision, and the confidence to push back on an attractive story when the evidence doesn't support it
Heavy, practical use of AI tools to move faster in your own work

Preferred Qualifications

Experience at a company that grew from bottoms-up adoption into enterprise sales (collaboration, productivity, or developer tools)
Consumption- or usage-based revenue models and PLG-to-sales motions (PQLs/PQAs, sales-assist)
Virality, network, or graph analysis of collaboration data
Fluency with Salesforce data and RevOps tooling
Modern data stack: BigQuery, dbt, Hex

Bonus Points

Experience with enterprise admin, security, or governance product surfaces
Built AI agents for GTM teams (account research, deal reviews, QBR prep)
Early member of an enterprise or GTM data function

Make architecture decisions with incomplete information and write down why you made them.

Associate Research Scientists develop their own research programs and also work in collaboration with ICC Research Scientists as well as postdoctoral fellows. Every tool you use was built as an island, so you became the glue between them: a name from Gmail into the CRM, a time from the CRM into Calendly, a note from Calendly into a doc. AI showed up and mostly became an eleventh window to paste into.
We're building a hybrid of AI and software standing on one shared brain. It holds your context and hands you real software built on top of it, so an ordinary scheduling tool becomes one that writes the invite itself and knows which of your busy hours bend, and for whom. Software for the path you repeat, AI for the edge that never repeats.
We're a team of about 15, backed by top-tier investors and Y Combinator, building from an office in the Presidio in San Francisco, a short walk from Crissy Field beach. We work absurdly hard because we can see and feel the outcome every day.

As a Senior Applied AI Engineer, you'll be responsible for building, refining, and scaling the agent systems inside our product, from architecture to evals to deployment. This is a senior seat. You own those systems, and when one breaks for a customer, that's on you.
We care about what works in production: fast response times, predictable behavior, traceability, and uptime.
A lot of what you'll decide has no playbook yet. We want someone who has already made calls like these on a real agent system and can tell us how they turned out.
You'll work across infra, frontend, and product to make sure the agents people build on our platform actually work, and you'll have a say in how the rest of the team builds them.

What you might work on?

Tool-using agents - multi-step agents that hit real APIs and handle retries, auth, timeouts, and edge cases.
Agent memory - systems that persist relevant state across runs: memory migrations, context organization, and orchestration state.
Proactive agents - agents that do work on their own and send you reminders.
Evals - own and evolve our eval framework, both automated checks and human-in-the-loop scoring.
Production debugging - dig into failures from traces and fix the underlying system.
Plus whatever else you see fit.

What we expect from you?

Pick the agent problems worth solving without waiting for a ticket.
Make architecture decisions with incomplete information and write down why you made them.
Decide what counts as reliable for our agents, and hold releases to it.
Review other people's code and design docs, and push the quality up.

What we're looking for?

This is a senior role. We're looking for someone who has run an agent system in production and made the architecture calls on it.
4+ years of engineering experience, including time shipping production software.
You've built and deployed agent-like systems: multi-step LLM pipelines, tool-using bots, scripted assistants, or similar.
You ran at least one of them in production, made the architecture calls on it, and can explain the tradeoffs.
Hands-on experience with:
Agent orchestration and memory management (e.g. memory migrations, state organization).
Tool use and orchestration (e.g. calling real APIs, using plugins, auth flows).
Evaluation: success metrics, regression testing, and improving agent behavior over time.
You write production-grade code and can work across systems without needing a spec.
You'd rather ship than polish forever.

Bonus (not required):
Shipped agents that live in the wild, used by customers, not just internal demos.
Familiarity with LLM ops, tracing, observability, and failure handling.
You've been a founder or early engineer, and it shows in the bar you hold your own work to.
You've mentored or led other engineers.

US work authorisation required; open to O-1 or J-1 visa sponsorship for exceptional candidates.

Exceptional candidates go from first touch to offer within two weeks.
